title: Module localization is the filtered colimit over powers
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, f an element of A, and M an A-module. The canonical map from the filtered colimit of the directed system M \xrightarrow{f} M \xrightarrow{f} M with every transition multiplication by f to the localization M_f [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is an isomorphism of A-modules; the class of m at stage e maps to m/f^e.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: Let C be the colimit of the sequence of copies of M with successive maps multiplication by f. The forgetful functor to additive commutative groups preserves this colimit, and the forgetful functor from additive commutative groups to types preserves filtered colimits. Thus every element of C has a stage representative, and equality of two stage representatives is witnessed at a common later stage.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: The colimit compatibility gives iota_(e+1)(f m) = iota_e(m). The maps m -> iota_(e+1)(m) also form a compatible cocone, inducing an endomorphism t of C. On stage representatives f t = id, and linearity implies t f = id. Therefore multiplication by f, and by every power of f, is invertible on C. Induction also gives iota_(e+k)(f^k m) = iota_e(m), and the transition from stage zero to stage k is multiplication by f^k.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: The map iota_0 : M -> C satisfies IsLocalizedModule for the powers of f. Invertibility is given by t. For x = iota_e(m), the transition formula gives f^e x = iota_0(m), which is the fraction-surjectivity condition. If iota_0(x) = iota_0(y), the filtered-colimit equality criterion gives a stage k where the two images agree. The transition formula says f^k x = f^k y, which is the localization equality condition.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: Apply Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.iso to iota_0 and take its inverse, obtaining C isomorphic to M_f. The formula iota_e(m) -> m/f^e follows from IsLocalizedModule.iso_symm_apply' and f^e iota_e(m) = iota_0(m). This formula characterizes the canonical map required in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem localization_away_colimit {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (f : R) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : let D : ℕ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R := Functor.ofSequence (X := fun _ : ℕ ↦ ModuleCat.of R M) (fun _ : ℕ ↦ ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.lsmul R M f)) ∃ κ : ↥(colimit D) ≃ₗ[R] LocalizedModule.Away f M, ∀ (e : ℕ) (m : M), κ ((colimit.ι D e) m) = LocalizedModule.mk (S := Submonoid.powers f) m ⟨f ^ e, ⟨e, rfl⟩⟩
